## Definition

The 7-layer skill architecture describes how Cohezion's ~258 installed capabilities (skills, commands, agents, MCP tools) are organized across 7 distinct source layers, each with different load mechanisms and token costs.

## The 7 Layers

| # | Layer | Location | Count | Load Mechanism |
|---|-------|----------|-------|----------------|
| 1 | BMAD Commands | `.claude/commands/bmad-*.md` | ~90 | Slash commands loading workflow `.md` |
| 2 | Project Commands | `.claude/commands/{audit,deploy,...}.md` | ~10 | Direct slash command execution |
| 3 | Project Skills | `.claude/skills/` | 1 | `Skill()` tool invocation |
| 4 | Global Commands | `~/.claude/commands/` | 7 | Structured workflow slash commands |
| 5 | Global Rules | `~/.claude/rules/*.md` | ~15 | Auto-loaded (enforcement, not invocable) |
| 6 | Plugin Skills | Marketplace + custom | ~55 | `Skill()` tool call |
| 7 | MCP Tools | `.mcp.json` + `~/.claude/mcp.json` | ~80 | `ToolSearch` then direct tool call |

**Effective unique capabilities:** ~198 (after removing ~60 redundant/duplicate entries).

## Key Properties

- **Token cost asymmetry**: Layers 1-4 are lightweight (3-6 lines each); Layer 6 plugins can have verbose descriptions; Layer 7 MCP tools are deferred (loaded only when needed)
- **Load timing**: Rules (Layer 5) load at session start; commands (1-4) load on invocation; plugins (6) load on `Skill()` call; MCP (7) loads on `ToolSearch`
- **Overlap zones**: BMAD BMM/GDS modules share ~12 skill names with domain variants; 3 plugin namespaces duplicate ~17 content creation skills each
- **Routing priority**: Exact match > lifecycle phase > domain > meta > creative > tool need

## BMAD Module Organization

BMAD (Layer 1) is subdivided into 5 modules:
- **BMM** — Business Model Module (product lifecycle: research → PRD → architecture → stories → dev → review)
- **GDS** — Game Development Studio (preproduction → design → technical → production → testing)
- **CIS** — Creative Innovation Studio (brainstorming, design thinking, innovation, storytelling)
- **TEA** — Test Engineering Academy (test design, automation, ATDD, CI, NFR, traceability)
- **BMB** — BMAD Module Builder (meta: create/edit/validate agents, workflows, modules)

## Relationship to Other Concepts

- [[agentic-ai]] — Skills are the action vocabulary of agentic systems
- [[workflow-orchestration]] — The routing decision tree is an orchestration pattern
- [[mcp-model-context-protocol]] — Layer 7; provides external data access for all other layers
- [[agent-architecture]] — Agent personas (Layer 1 agents) define role-based expertise domains

- Full taxonomy: `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/research/technical-skills-taxonomy-research-2026-03-07.md`
- Routing pattern: [[skill-routing-decision-tree]]
- Skills index: `~/vaults/cohezion-vault/skills_index/`

# Decision: Skill Pruning & Consolidation Plan

## Context

After taxonomizing all 258 installed capabilities across 7 source layers, analysis reveals ~60 redundant or dormant entries inflating the skill listing by ~40%. This noise increases routing ambiguity and wastes tokens on skill enumeration.

## Decision

### Phase 1: Remove Triple-Duplicate Plugin Skills (Immediate)

Remove 2 of 3 identical plugin namespaces:
- **Keep:** `document-skills:*` (canonical namespace)
- **Remove:** `claude-api:*` (~17 skills, identical to document-skills)
- **Remove:** `example-skills:*` (~17 skills, identical to document-skills)

**Impact:** -34 redundant entries, zero capability loss.

### Phase 2: Consolidate Review Skills (Short-term)

| Current | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `code-review:code-review` | Remove (subset of `pr-review-toolkit:review-pr`) |
| `bmad-gds-code-review` | Disable unless game project active |

### Phase 3: Disable Dormant GDS Skills (When No Game Project)

The GDS module adds ~20 commands + 7 agent personas that are irrelevant unless actively building a game. Recommend a "game mode" toggle:
- Default: GDS commands hidden from routing
- When game project detected (e.g., `_bmad/gds/` populated): auto-enable

### Phase 4: Evaluate Low-Signal Plugins

| Plugin | Recommendation |
|--------|----------------|
| `ralph-loop:*` | Remove if unused after 30 days |
| `sentry:*` | Keep dormant; auto-enable when Sentry DSN configured |
| `hookify:writing-rules` | Remove (covered by `hookify:hookify`) |

## Expected Impact

- **Token savings:** ~60 fewer entries in skill listing = reduced enumeration noise
- **Routing clarity:** Fewer ambiguous overlaps = faster, more accurate skill selection
- **Reversibility:** All removals are plugin uninstalls or command renames — fully reversible

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Do nothing** — Accept the noise. Rejected: token costs compound across every session.
2. **Merge all content skills into one namespace** — Would require plugin refactoring. Deferred.
3. **Dynamic loading based on project type** — Best long-term solution but requires infrastructure. Deferred to Phase 3.

## Related

- [[skill-taxonomy-7-layer-architecture]]
- [[skill-routing-decision-tree]]
- Full analysis: `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/research/technical-skills-taxonomy-research-2026-03-07.md`

# /learn - Online Learning System

**Extract reusable knowledge from this session into skills.** Evaluates what was learned, checks for existing skills, and creates new ones when valuable patterns are discovered.

---

## TABLE OF CONTENTS

| Phase       | Description                                            | Steps   |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------- |
| **Phase 0** | Reference: triggers, quality criteria, skill structure | 0.1–0.4 |
| **Phase 1** | Evaluate: assess if knowledge is worth extracting      | 1.1     |
| **Phase 2** | Check Existing: search for related skills              | 2.1     |
| **Phase 3** | Create Skill: write the skill file                     | 3.1–3.2 |
| **Phase 4** | Quality Gates: final checklist before saving           | 4.1     |

**Quick Step Reference:**

- 0.1 Triggers, 0.2 Quality criteria, 0.3 What NOT to extract, 0.4 Skill structure
- 1.1 Self-evaluation questions
- 2.1 Search existing skills
- 3.1 Choose location, 3.2 Write SKILL.md
- 4.1 Final checklist

---

## PHASE 0: REFERENCE

### Step 0.1: Triggers

Invoke `/learn` after ANY task involving:

| Trigger                      | Example                                                          |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Non-obvious debugging**    | Spent 10+ minutes investigating; solution wasn't in docs         |
| **Misleading errors**        | Error message pointed wrong direction; found real cause          |
| **Workarounds**              | Found limitation and creative solution                           |
| **Tool integration**         | Figured out how to use tool/API in undocumented way              |
| **Trial-and-error**          | Tried multiple approaches before finding what worked             |
| **Repeatable workflow**      | Multi-step task that will recur; worth standardizing             |
| **External service queries** | Fetched data from Jira, GitHub, Confluence, or other APIs        |
| **User-facing automation**   | Built something user will ask for again (reports, status checks) |

### Step 0.2: Quality Criteria

Skills must be:

- **Reusable**: Will help with future tasks (not just this instance)
- **Non-trivial**: Required discovery, OR is a valuable workflow pattern
- **Verified**: Solution actually worked, not theoretical

### Step 0.3: What NOT to Extract

- Single-step tasks with no workflow value
- One-off fixes unlikely to recur
- Knowledge easily found in official docs

### Step 0.4: Skill Structure

**Location:** `.claude/skills/[skill-name]/SKILL.md`

**Template:**

```markdown
---
name: descriptive-kebab-case-name
description: |
  [CRITICAL: This determines when the skill triggers. Include:]
  - What the skill does
  - Specific trigger conditions (exact error messages, symptoms)
  - When to use it (contexts, scenarios)
author: Claude Code
version: 1.0.0
---

# Skill Name

## Problem

[Clear description of the problem]

## Context / Trigger Conditions

[When to use - exact error messages, symptoms, scenarios]

## Solution

[Step-by-step solution]

## Verification

[How to verify it worked]

## Example

[Concrete example]

## References

[Links to documentation]
```

<details>
<summary>Writing Effective Descriptions</summary>

The description field is CRITICAL for skill discovery:

**Good:**

```yaml
description: |
  Fix for "ENOENT: no such file or directory" errors in npm monorepos.
  Use when: (1) npm run fails with ENOENT, (2) paths work in root but
  not in packages, (3) symlinked dependencies cause failures.
```

**Bad:**

```yaml
description: Helps with npm problems in monorepos.
```

</details>

**Guidelines:**

- **Concise** - Claude is smart; only add what it doesn't know
- **Under 500 lines** - Move large docs to `references/`
- **Examples over explanations** - Show, don't tell

---

## PHASE 1: EVALUATE

### Step 1.1: Self-Evaluation Questions

Ask yourself:

1. "What did I just learn that wasn't obvious before starting?"
2. "Would future-me benefit from having this documented?"
3. "Was the solution non-obvious from documentation alone?"
4. "Is this a multi-step workflow I'd repeat on similar tasks?"
5. "Did I query an external service the user will ask about again?"

**If NO to all → Skip extraction, nothing to learn.**

**Note:** External service queries (Jira tickets, GitHub PRs, Confluence pages) are almost always worth extracting - users frequently repeat these requests.

---

## PHASE 2: CHECK EXISTING

### Step 2.1: Search for Related Skills

Before creating, search for related skills:

```bash
ls .claude/skills/ 2>/dev/null
rg -i "keyword" .claude/skills/ 2>/dev/null
ls ~/.claude/pilot/skills/ 2>/dev/null
rg -i "keyword" ~/.claude/pilot/skills/ 2>/dev/null
```

| Found                | Action                           |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Nothing related      | Create new skill                 |
| Same trigger and fix | Update existing (bump version)   |
| Partial overlap      | Update existing with new variant |

---

## PHASE 3: CREATE SKILL

### Step 3.1: Choose Location

**Project skills**: `.claude/skills/[skill-name]/SKILL.md`

### Step 3.2: Write SKILL.md

Use the template from Step 0.4. Ensure the description field contains specific trigger conditions.

---

## PHASE 4: QUALITY GATES

### Step 4.1: Final Checklist

Before finalizing:

- [ ] Description contains specific trigger conditions
- [ ] Solution verified to work
- [ ] Content specific enough to be actionable
- [ ] Content general enough to be reusable
- [ ] No sensitive information

---

## EXAMPLE

**Scenario**: Discovered LSP `findReferences` can find dead code by checking if functions have only 1 reference (their definition) or only test references.

**Skill Created**: `.claude/skills/lsp-dead-code-finder/SKILL.md`

```markdown
---
name: lsp-dead-code-finder
description: |
  Find dead/unused code using LSP findReferences. Use when: (1) user asks
  to find dead code, (2) cleaning up codebase, (3) refactoring. Key insight:
  function with only 1 reference (definition) or only test refs is dead code.
---

# LSP Dead Code Finder

...
```

---

## REMEMBER

**Continuous improvement.** Every valuable discovery should benefit future sessions.
Evaluate after significant work. Extract selectively. Create carefully.

   188→
   189→## Routing Strategy: Natural Language → Skill
   190→
   191→### Decision Tree (Priority Order)
   192→
   193→```
   194→User says something →
   195→  1. EXACT MATCH: Does it match a slash command? → Execute directly
   196→  2. LIFECYCLE PHASE: What phase of work is this?
   197→     ├─ Research/Analysis → BMM research or CIS brainstorming
   198→     ├─ Planning/Design → BMM PRD/Architecture or GDS Brief/GDD
   199→     ├─ Implementation → BMM dev-story/quick-dev or spec workflow
   200→     ├─ Testing → TEA testarch-* or test-fix
   201→     ├─ Review → bmad-review-* or code-review
   202→     └─ Maintenance → retrospect, correct-course, deploy, heal
   203→  3. DOMAIN: Is this game dev? → GDS variant. General product? → BMM variant.
   204→  4. META: Is this about BMAD itself? → BMB module
   205→  5. CREATIVE: Is this ideation/innovation? → CIS module
   206→  6. TOOL NEED: Does it need external data?
   207→     ├─ Library docs → context7
   208→     ├─ Research papers → cohezion-research
   209→     ├─ GitHub code → github MCP
   210→     ├─ Knowledge graph → cohezion-surreal
   211→     └─ Multi-perspective → cohezion-swarm
   212→```
   213→
   214→### Keyword Routing Map

   223→| "implement", "build", "code this" | `bmad-bmm-dev-story` | `bmad-bmm-quick-dev` |
   224→| "test", "testing", "QA" | `bmad-tea-testarch-test-design` | `test-fix` |

   230→| "commit", "push", "PR" | `commit-commands:*` | — |
   231→| "what now", "help", "next step" | `bmad-help` | — |

   233→
   234→### Overlap Resolution (Same Intent, Multiple Skills)
   235→
   236→| Ambiguity | Resolution Rule |
   237→|-----------|-----------------|
   238→| `bmad-bmm-code-review` vs `code-review:code-review` vs `bmad-gds-code-review` | BMM for product code, GDS for game code, `code-review` plugin for PR-focused review |
   239→| `bmad-bmm-quick-dev` vs `bmad-gds-quick-dev` | Domain context: game project → GDS, otherwise → BMM |
   240→| `bmad-bmm-sprint-planning` vs `bmad-gds-sprint-planning` | Same: domain context decides |
   241→| `bmad-brainstorming` vs `bmad-cis-brainstorming` vs `superpowers:brainstorming` | `superpowers` is a meta-prompt enhancer; `bmad-brainstorming` is the interactive workflow; `bmad-cis-brainstorming` is a lighter MCP variant |
   242→| `bmad-bmm-retrospective` vs `bmad-gds-retrospective` vs `retrospect` | `retrospect` is dev-focused (flows into core files); BMAD variants are product/game lifecycle |
   243→| `spec` vs `bmad-bmm-quick-spec` vs `bmad-gds-quick-spec` | `/spec` is a full structured workflow with TDD; `quick-spec` is lightweight for small changes |
   244→| `bmad-bmm-create-story` vs `bmad-gds-create-story` | Domain context |
   245→
   246→## Key Relationships
   247→
   248→### Lifecycle Flow (BMM)
   249→```
   250→research → product-brief → PRD → architecture → UX-design
   251→  → epics-and-stories → sprint-planning → dev-story → code-review
   252→  → sprint-status → retrospective
   253→```
   254→

   256→```

   258→  → sprint-planning → create-story → dev-story → code-review
   259→  → gametest-* → sprint-status → retrospective

   265→create-agent / create-workflow (independently)

   272→Superpowers are **meta-skills** that wrap around other skills:
   273→- `brainstorming` → runs before creative BMAD/CIS skills
   274→- `systematic-debugging` → runs before `test-fix`
   275→- `test-driven-development` → runs during `dev-story` / `spec-implement`
   276→- `verification-before-completion` → runs after any implementation
   277→
   278→## Pruning Recommendations
   279→
   280→### Redundant / Consolidation Candidates
   281→
   282→| Skill(s) | Issue | Recommendation |
   283→|-----------|-------|----------------|
   284→| `bmad-gds-create-game-brief` + `bmad-gds-game-brief` | Two skills for the same thing (one via MCP, one via command) | Keep command version, remove MCP duplicate |
   285→| `bmad-gds-gdd` + `bmad-gds-create-gdd` | Same — GDD creation via two paths | Keep `create-gdd` (collaborative), deprecate `gdd` |
   286→| `bmad-brainstorming` + `bmad-cis-brainstorming` + `superpowers:brainstorming` | Three brainstorming skills | Keep `bmad-brainstorming` (interactive workflow) + `superpowers:brainstorming` (meta-enhancer). Remove MCP `cis-brainstorming` |
   287→| `bmad-bmm-code-review` + `bmad-gds-code-review` + `code-review:code-review` + `pr-review-toolkit:review-pr` | Four code review skills | Keep `bmad-bmm-code-review` (general) + `pr-review-toolkit:review-pr` (PR-specific). Remove `gds-code-review` unless actively building games. Remove `code-review:code-review` (subset of pr-review-toolkit) |
   288→| `bmad-bmm-sprint-status` + `bmad-gds-sprint-status` | Duplicate sprint status for two domains | Keep BMM, alias GDS to it unless game project active |
   289→| `bmad-bmm-retrospective` + `bmad-gds-retrospective` + `retrospect` | Three retro skills | Keep `retrospect` (dev-focused, flows into core files) + `bmad-bmm-retrospective` (product lifecycle). Remove GDS variant |
   290→| `claude-api:*` + `document-skills:*` + `example-skills:*` | Three plugin namespaces with identical skills (pdf, docx, pptx, frontend-design, etc.) | These are the same skills from different marketplace plugins. Keep ONE namespace (recommend `document-skills:*`), remove the other two |
   291→
   292→### Low-Value / Never-Used Candidates
   293→
   294→| Skill | Reason | Recommendation |
   295→|-------|--------|----------------|
   296→| `bmad-bmb-validate-max-parallel-workflow` | Extremely niche — only for parallel workflow validation | Keep only if actively building BMAD modules |
   297→| `bmad-gds-gametest-*` (6 skills) | Full game testing suite — irrelevant unless building games | Disable unless game project active |
   298→| `bmad-agent-gds-*` (7 agents) | Game-specific agent personas | Same — disable unless game project |
   299→| `hookify:writing-rules` | Meta-skill about writing hookify rules | Rarely needed; `hookify:hookify` covers creation |
   300→| `ralph-loop:*` (3 skills) | Ralph Loop plugin — unclear if used | Evaluate usage; remove if unused |
   301→| `sentry:*` (3 skills) | Sentry integration — only relevant if using Sentry | Keep dormant unless Sentry is configured |
   302→| `huggingface-skills:*` (12 skills) | HuggingFace ecosystem — heavy, niche | Keep only if doing ML model work |
   303→
   304→### Token Cost Analysis
   305→
   306→The biggest token sinks from skill/command loading:
   307→1. **BMAD commands** (~90): Each is tiny (3-6 lines), but they all appear in the skill listing, adding noise
   308→2. **Triple-duplicate plugin skills** (claude-api + document-skills + example-skills): ~40 skills x3 = 120 entries for ~40 actual capabilities
   309→3. **GDS module** (~20 skills): Full game dev pipeline that's dormant unless building games
   310→
   311→**Estimated savings from pruning**: Remove ~60 redundant/dormant entries, reducing skill listing noise by ~40%.
   312→
   313→## Implementation Plan
   314→
   315→### Task 1: Add CLAUDE.md Skill Routing Section (Highest Compound Value)
   316→**File:** `CLAUDE.md`
   317→
   318→Add a condensed `## Skill Routing Quick Reference` section (~50 lines) containing:
   319→- The 6-step decision tree (exact match → lifecycle → domain → meta → creative → tool)
   320→- Top 15 keyword→skill mappings (the ones used most)
   321→- Overlap resolution rules (5 key ambiguities)
   322→- "When in doubt" default: `bmad-help`
   323→
   324→This section goes in CLAUDE.md so it loads automatically every session. Keep it under 100 lines to respect token budgets.
   325→
   326→### Task 2: Write Full Research Document
   327→**File:** `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/research/technical-skills-taxonomy-research-2026-03-07.md`
   328→
   329→Full BMAD research template with:
   330→- Complete taxonomy (all 7 source layers)
   331→- Relationship diagrams (lifecycle flows)
   332→- Routing strategy (decision tree + keyword map)
   333→- Pruning recommendations with rationale
   334→- Overlap resolution matrix
   335→
   336→### Task 3: Store Taxonomy in Obsidian Vault
   337→**Target directories in** `~/vaults/cohezion-vault/`:
   338→
   339→| Artifact | Vault Path | Purpose |
   340→|----------|------------|---------|
   341→| Routing pattern | `patterns/skill-routing-decision-tree.md` | Reusable pattern using vault template format (type, category, frequency, confidence, code_example) |
   342→| Taxonomy concept | `concepts/skill-taxonomy-7-layer-architecture.md` | Concept note with MOC links to existing `agentic-ai.md`, `workflow-orchestration.md`, `mcp-model-context-protocol.md` |

# Technical Research: Installed Skills Taxonomy & Natural Language Routing

## Context

Cohezion has accumulated **150+ skills, commands, agents, and MCP tools** from 7 distinct sources. There is no unified map showing how they relate or which to invoke for a given natural language request. This research produces that map — a complete taxonomy with routing heuristics.

## Skill Sources (7 Layers)

| # | Source | Location | Count | Load Mechanism |
|---|--------|----------|-------|----------------|
| 1 | **BMAD Commands** (project) | `.claude/commands/bmad-*.md` | ~90 | Slash commands → load workflow `.md` from `_bmad/` |
| 2 | **Project Commands** (custom) | `.claude/commands/{audit,async-audit,bash-report}.md` | 3 | Slash commands → direct execution |
| 3 | **Project Skills** | `.claude/skills/update-tools/` | 1 | Skill invocation |
| 4 | **Global Commands** (Pilot) | `~/.claude/commands/{spec,spec-plan,spec-implement,spec-verify,sync,learn,vault}.md` | 7 | Slash commands — structured workflows |
| 5 | **Global Rules** (Pilot) | `~/.claude/rules/*.md` | ~15 | Auto-loaded at session start — enforcement, not invocable |
| 6 | **Plugin Skills** (marketplace) | Loaded via `/plugin marketplace add` | ~40 | `Skill()` tool — registered in session |
| 7 | **MCP Tools** | `.mcp.json` + `~/.claude/mcp.json` | ~80 | `ToolSearch` → direct tool call |

## BMAD Module Taxonomy (The Big One — ~90 commands)

BMAD is organized into **5 modules**, each with a lifecycle phase focus:

### BMM — Business Model Module (Product Lifecycle)
**Prefix:** `bmad-bmm-*` | **Workflows in:** `_bmad/bmm/workflows/`

| Phase | Skills | Natural Language Triggers |
|-------|--------|--------------------------|
| **1-Analysis** | `technical-research`, `domain-research`, `market-research` | "research X", "investigate Y", "what are the options for Z" |
| **2-Planning** | `create-prd`, `edit-prd`, `validate-prd`, `create-product-brief`, `create-architecture`, `create-ux-design` | "create a PRD", "design the architecture", "plan the UX" |
| **3-Solutioning** | `create-epics-and-stories`, `create-story`, `sprint-planning`, `sprint-status` | "break this into stories", "plan the sprint", "check sprint status" |
| **4-Implementation** | `dev-story`, `quick-dev`, `quick-spec`, `code-review` | "implement story X", "quick fix", "review this code" |
| **Cross-cutting** | `check-implementation-readiness`, `correct-course`, `retrospective`, `document-project`, `generate-project-context` | "are we ready to build?", "course correct", "run retro", "document this project" |

### GDS — Game Development Studio
**Prefix:** `bmad-gds-*` | **Workflows in:** `_bmad/gds/workflows/`

| Phase | Skills | Natural Language Triggers |
|-------|--------|--------------------------|
| **1-Preproduction** | `create-game-brief`, `game-brief`, `brainstorm-game` | "let's brainstorm a game", "create game brief" |
| **2-Design** | `gdd`, `create-gdd`, `narrative` | "create game design doc", "write narrative" |
| **3-Technical** | `game-architecture`, `quick-spec`, `quick-dev` | "design game architecture", "quick game spec" |
| **4-Production** | `dev-story`, `create-story`, `sprint-planning`, `sprint-status`, `code-review`, `correct-course`, `retrospective` | "implement game story", "game sprint status" |
| **Testing** | `gametest-framework`, `gametest-test-design`, `gametest-automate`, `gametest-test-review`, `gametest-playtest-plan`, `gametest-performance` | "create test framework", "design game tests", "playtest plan" |

### CIS — Creative Innovation Studio
**Prefix:** `bmad-cis-*` | **Workflows in:** `_bmad/cis/workflows/`

| Skills | Natural Language Triggers |
|--------|--------------------------|
| `brainstorming` (+ `bmad-brainstorming`) | "let's brainstorm", "ideation session" |
| `design-thinking` | "design thinking workshop", "empathy mapping" |
| `innovation-strategy` | "disruption analysis", "innovation opportunities" |
| `problem-solving` | "systematic problem solving", "root cause analysis" |
| `storytelling` | "craft a narrative", "tell a story about X" |

### TEA — Test Engineering Academy
**Prefix:** `bmad-tea-*` | **Workflows in:** `_bmad/tea/workflows/`

| Skills | Natural Language Triggers |
|--------|--------------------------|
| `testarch-test-design` | "design test plan", "test strategy" |
| `testarch-automate` | "expand test automation", "automate tests" |
| `testarch-atdd` | "acceptance test driven", "write acceptance tests" |
| `testarch-test-review` | "review test quality" |
| `testarch-framework` | "setup test framework", "init Playwright/Cypress" |
| `testarch-ci` | "setup CI pipeline", "quality gates" |
| `testarch-nfr` | "assess NFRs", "performance/security assessment" |
| `testarch-trace` | "traceability matrix", "quality gate decision" |
| `teach-me-testing` | "teach me testing", "learn testing" |

### BMB — BMAD Module Builder (Meta)
**Prefix:** `bmad-bmb-*` | **Workflows in:** `_bmad/bmb/workflows/`

| Skills | Natural Language Triggers |
|--------|--------------------------|
| `create-agent`, `edit-agent`, `validate-agent` | "create a BMAD agent", "validate agent" |
| `create-workflow`, `edit-workflow`, `validate-workflow`, `rework-workflow` | "create workflow", "validate workflow" |
| `create-module`, `edit-module`, `validate-module`, `create-module-brief` | "create BMAD module", "validate module" |
| `validate-max-parallel-workflow` | "validate workflow in parallel mode" |

### BMAD Cross-Cutting Utilities
| Skill | Natural Language Triggers |
|-------|--------------------------|
| `bmad-help` | "what should I do next", "help me", "what now" |
| `bmad-party-mode` | "party mode", "group discussion with all agents" |
| `bmad-index-docs` | "index the docs", "generate doc index" |
| `bmad-shard-doc` | "split this document", "shard large markdown" |
| `bmad-editorial-review-prose` | "review for prose quality", "copy edit" |
| `bmad-editorial-review-structure` | "review document structure", "structural edit" |
| `bmad-review-adversarial-general` | "cynical review", "adversarial review" |
| `bmad-review-edge-case-hunter` | "find edge cases", "boundary condition review" |

### BMAD Agent Personas (~20 agents)
**Prefix:** `bmad-agent-*` — These are role-based personas, not workflows.

| Domain | Agents |
|--------|--------|
| BMM | `architect`, `dev`, `qa`, `sm`, `pm`, `analyst`, `tech-writer`, `ux-designer`, `quick-flow-solo-dev` |
| GDS | `game-architect`, `game-designer`, `game-dev`, `game-qa`, `game-scrum-master`, `game-solo-dev`, `tech-writer` |
| CIS | `brainstorming-coach`, `creative-problem-solver`, `design-thinking-coach`, `innovation-strategist`, `presentation-master`, `storyteller` |
| TEA | `tea` |
| BMB | `agent-builder`, `module-builder`, `workflow-builder` |
| Core | `bmad-master` |

## Plugin Skills (Marketplace & Custom)

### Development Workflow
| Skill | Trigger | Source |

## MCP Tool Servers (7 servers, ~80 tools)

## Routing Strategy: Natural Language → Skill

### Decision Tree (Priority Order)

```
User says something →
  1. EXACT MATCH: Does it match a slash command? → Execute directly
  2. LIFECYCLE PHASE: What phase of work is this?
     ├─ Research/Analysis → BMM research or CIS brainstorming
     ├─ Planning/Design → BMM PRD/Architecture or GDS Brief/GDD
     ├─ Implementation → BMM dev-story/quick-dev or spec workflow
     ├─ Testing → TEA testarch-* or test-fix
     ├─ Review → bmad-review-* or code-review
     └─ Maintenance → retrospect, correct-course, deploy, heal
  3. DOMAIN: Is this game dev? → GDS variant. General product? → BMM variant.
  4. META: Is this about BMAD itself? → BMB module
  5. CREATIVE: Is this ideation/innovation? → CIS module
  6. TOOL NEED: Does it need external data?
     ├─ Library docs → context7
     ├─ Research papers → cohezion-research
     ├─ GitHub code → github MCP
     ├─ Knowledge graph → cohezion-surreal
     └─ Multi-perspective → cohezion-swarm
```

### Keyword Routing Map

| Keywords in Request | Primary Skill | Fallback |
|---------------------|---------------|----------|
| "research", "investigate", "explore options" | `bmad-bmm-technical-research` | `bmad-bmm-domain-research` |
| "PRD", "requirements", "product spec" | `bmad-bmm-create-prd` | `bmad-bmm-edit-prd` |
| "architecture", "system design" | `bmad-bmm-create-architecture` | `bmad-gds-game-architecture` |
| "story", "epic", "user story" | `bmad-bmm-create-story` | `bmad-bmm-create-epics-and-stories` |
| "sprint", "planning" | `bmad-bmm-sprint-planning` | `bmad-bmm-sprint-status` |
| "implement", "build", "code this" | `bmad-bmm-dev-story` | `bmad-bmm-quick-dev` |
| "test", "testing", "QA" | `bmad-tea-testarch-test-design` | `test-fix` |
| "review", "code review" | `bmad-bmm-code-review` | `code-review:code-review` |
| "brainstorm", "ideate" | `bmad-brainstorming` | `bmad-cis-brainstorming` |
| "game", "gameplay" | Route to `bmad-gds-*` variant | — |
| "deploy", "ship" | `deploy` | — |
| "fix tests", "failing tests" | `test-fix` | — |
| "commit", "push", "PR" | `commit-commands:*` | — |
| "what now", "help", "next step" | `bmad-help` | — |
| "spec", "structured dev" | `/spec` | — |

### Overlap Resolution (Same Intent, Multiple Skills)

| Ambiguity | Resolution Rule |
|-----------|-----------------|
| `bmad-bmm-code-review` vs `code-review:code-review` vs `bmad-gds-code-review` | BMM for product code, GDS for game code, `code-review` plugin for PR-focused review |
| `bmad-bmm-quick-dev` vs `bmad-gds-quick-dev` | Domain context: game project → GDS, otherwise → BMM |
| `bmad-bmm-sprint-planning` vs `bmad-gds-sprint-planning` | Same: domain context decides |
| `bmad-brainstorming` vs `bmad-cis-brainstorming` vs `superpowers:brainstorming` | `superpowers` is a meta-prompt enhancer; `bmad-brainstorming` is the interactive workflow; `bmad-cis-brainstorming` is a lighter MCP variant |
| `bmad-bmm-retrospective` vs `bmad-gds-retrospective` vs `retrospect` | `retrospect` is dev-focused (flows into core files); BMAD variants are product/game lifecycle |
| `spec` vs `bmad-bmm-quick-spec` vs `bmad-gds-quick-spec` | `/spec` is a full structured workflow with TDD; `quick-spec` is lightweight for small changes |
| `bmad-bmm-create-story` vs `bmad-gds-create-story` | Domain context |

## Key Relationships

### Lifecycle Flow (BMM)
```
research → product-brief → PRD → architecture → UX-design
  → epics-and-stories → sprint-planning → dev-story → code-review
  → sprint-status → retrospective
```

### Lifecycle Flow (GDS)
```
brainstorm-game → game-brief → GDD → narrative → game-architecture
  → sprint-planning → create-story → dev-story → code-review
  → gametest-* → sprint-status → retrospective
```

### Meta Flow (BMB)
```
create-module-brief → create-module
create-agent / create-workflow (independently)
validate-agent / validate-workflow / validate-module (quality gates)
edit-agent / edit-workflow / edit-module (modifications)
rework-workflow (V6 compliance upgrade)
```

### Superpowers Integration
Superpowers are **meta-skills** that wrap around other skills:
- `brainstorming` → runs before creative BMAD/CIS skills
- `systematic-debugging` → runs before `test-fix`
- `test-driven-development` → runs during `dev-story` / `spec-implement`
- `verification-before-completion` → runs after any implementation

## Pruning Recommendations

### Redundant / Consolidation Candidates

| Skill(s) | Issue | Recommendation |
|-----------|-------|----------------|
| `bmad-gds-create-game-brief` + `bmad-gds-game-brief` | Two skills for the same thing (one via MCP, one via command) | Keep command version, remove MCP duplicate |
| `bmad-gds-gdd` + `bmad-gds-create-gdd` | Same — GDD creation via two paths | Keep `create-gdd` (collaborative), deprecate `gdd` |
| `bmad-brainstorming` + `bmad-cis-brainstorming` + `superpowers:brainstorming` | Three brainstorming skills | Keep `bmad-brainstorming` (interactive workflow) + `superpowers:brainstorming` (meta-enhancer). Remove MCP `cis-brainstorming` |
| `bmad-bmm-code-review` + `bmad-gds-code-review` + `code-review:code-review` + `pr-review-toolkit:review-pr` | Four code review skills | Keep `bmad-bmm-code-review` (general) + `pr-review-toolkit:review-pr` (PR-specific). Remove `gds-code-review` unless actively building games. Remove `code-review:code-review` (subset of pr-review-toolkit) |
| `bmad-bmm-sprint-status` + `bmad-gds-sprint-status` | Duplicate sprint status for two domains | Keep BMM, alias GDS to it unless game project active |
| `bmad-bmm-retrospective` + `bmad-gds-retrospective` + `retrospect` | Three retro skills | Keep `retrospect` (dev-focused, flows into core files) + `bmad-bmm-retrospective` (product lifecycle). Remove GDS variant |
| `claude-api:*` + `document-skills:*` + `example-skills:*` | Three plugin namespaces with identical skills (pdf, docx, pptx, frontend-design, etc.) | These are the same skills from different marketplace plugins. Keep ONE namespace (recommend `document-skills:*`), remove the other two |

### Low-Value / Never-Used Candidates

| Skill | Reason | Recommendation |
|-------|--------|----------------|
| `bmad-bmb-validate-max-parallel-workflow` | Extremely niche — only for parallel workflow validation | Keep only if actively building BMAD modules |
| `bmad-gds-gametest-*` (6 skills) | Full game testing suite — irrelevant unless building games | Disable unless game project active |
| `bmad-agent-gds-*` (7 agents) | Game-specific agent personas | Same — disable unless game project |
| `hookify:writing-rules` | Meta-skill about writing hookify rules | Rarely needed; `hookify:hookify` covers creation |
| `ralph-loop:*` (3 skills) | Ralph Loop plugin — unclear if used | Evaluate usage; remove if unused |
| `sentry:*` (3 skills) | Sentry integration — only relevant if using Sentry | Keep dormant unless Sentry is configured |
| `huggingface-skills:*` (12 skills) | HuggingFace ecosystem — heavy, niche | Keep only if doing ML model work |

### Token Cost Analysis

The biggest token sinks from skill/command loading:
1. **BMAD commands** (~90): Each is tiny (3-6 lines), but they all appear in the skill listing, adding noise
2. **Triple-duplicate plugin skills** (claude-api + document-skills + example-skills): ~40 skills x3 = 120 entries for ~40 actual capabilities
3. **GDS module** (~20 skills): Full game dev pipeline that's dormant unless building games

**Estimated savings from pruning**: Remove ~60 redundant/dormant entries, reducing skill listing noise by ~40%.

## Implementation Plan

### Task 1: Add CLAUDE.md Skill Routing Section (Highest Compound Value)
**File:** `CLAUDE.md`

Add a condensed `## Skill Routing Quick Reference` section (~50 lines) containing:
- The 6-step decision tree (exact match → lifecycle → domain → meta → creative → tool)
- Top 15 keyword→skill mappings (the ones used most)
- Overlap resolution rules (5 key ambiguities)
- "When in doubt" default: `bmad-help`

This section goes in CLAUDE.md so it loads automatically every session. Keep it under 100 lines to respect token budgets.

### Task 2: Write Full Research Document
**File:** `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/research/technical-skills-taxonomy-research-2026-03-07.md`

Full BMAD research template with:
- Complete taxonomy (all 7 source layers)
- Relationship diagrams (lifecycle flows)
- Routing strategy (decision tree + keyword map)
- Pruning recommendations with rationale
- Overlap resolution matrix

### Task 3: Store Taxonomy in Obsidian Vault
**Target directories in** `~/vaults/cohezion-vault/`:

| Artifact | Vault Path | Purpose |
|----------|------------|---------|
| Routing pattern | `patterns/skill-routing-decision-tree.md` | Reusable pattern using vault template format (type, category, frequency, confidence, code_example) |
| Taxonomy concept | `concepts/skill-taxonomy-7-layer-architecture.md` | Concept note with MOC links to existing `agentic-ai.md`, `workflow-orchestration.md`, `mcp-model-context-protocol.md` |
| Pruning decision | `decisions/2026-03-07-skill-pruning-consolidation-plan.md` | Decision record: what to prune, why, expected impact |
| Skills index | `skills_index/` | Populate the currently-empty directory with per-module index files (bmm.md, gds.md, cis.md, tea.md, bmb.md, plugins.md) |

Use vault templates (`templates/pattern.md`) for pattern notes. Include Obsidian wiki-links (`[[concept-name]]`) to connect to existing vault knowledge.

### Task 4: Store Key Learnings in SurrealDB
Use `mcp__cohezion-surreal__store_learning` and `mcp__cohezion-surreal__store_node` to persist:

| Learning ID | Title | Content Summary | Score |
|-------------|-------|-----------------|-------|
| `skill-taxonomy-2026-03-07` | "7-Layer Skill Architecture" | Complete source map: BMAD commands, project skills, global commands, rules, plugins, MCP tools | 0.95 |
| `skill-routing-strategy` | "Natural Language to Skill Routing" | Decision tree: exact match -> lifecycle -> domain -> meta -> creative -> tool need | 0.9 |
| `skill-pruning-analysis` | "Skill Redundancy Analysis" | 60+ redundant entries from triple-duplicate plugins, dormant GDS module, overlapping reviews | 0.85 |
| `skill-overlap-resolution` | "Skill Overlap Resolution Rules" | 7 key ambiguities with resolution: domain context, scope (PR vs general), lifecycle phase | 0.8 |

Also store a `document` node with the full taxonomy for vector similarity search.

### Task 5: Clean Up Triple-Duplicate Plugin Skills
Remove 2 of the 3 duplicate plugin namespaces (`claude-api:*`, `document-skills:*`, `example-skills:*`). Keep `document-skills:*` as the canonical namespace.

## Verification

1. `grep -c "Skill Routing" CLAUDE.md` -- confirm section exists
2. Count skills before/after pruning: `ls .claude/commands/ | wc -l`
3. Spot-check routing: test 5 natural language phrases against the decision tree

# Technical Research: Installed Skills Taxonomy & Natural Language Routing

## Context

Cohezion has accumulated **150+ skills, commands, agents, and MCP tools** from 7 distinct sources. There is no unified map showing how they relate or which to invoke for a given natural language request. This research produces that map — a complete taxonomy with routing heuristics.

## Skill Sources (7 Layers)

| # | Source | Location | Count | Load Mechanism |
|---|--------|----------|-------|----------------|
| 1 | **BMAD Commands** (project) | `.claude/commands/bmad-*.md` | ~90 | Slash commands → load workflow `.md` from `_bmad/` |
| 2 | **Project Commands** (custom) | `.claude/commands/{audit,async-audit,bash-report}.md` | 3 | Slash commands → direct execution |
| 3 | **Project Skills** | `.claude/skills/update-tools/` | 1 | Skill invocation |
| 4 | **Global Commands** (Pilot) | `~/.claude/commands/{spec,spec-plan,spec-implement,spec-verify,sync,learn,vault}.md` | 7 | Slash commands — structured workflows |
| 5 | **Global Rules** (Pilot) | `~/.claude/rules/*.md` | ~15 | Auto-loaded at session start — enforcement, not invocable |
| 6 | **Plugin Skills** (marketplace) | Loaded via `/plugin marketplace add` | ~40 | `Skill()` tool — registered in session |
| 7 | **MCP Tools** | `.mcp.json` + `~/.claude/mcp.json` | ~80 | `ToolSearch` → direct tool call |

## BMAD Module Taxonomy (The Big One — ~90 commands)

BMAD is organized into **5 modules**, each with a lifecycle phase focus:

### BMM — Business Model Module (Product Lifecycle)
**Prefix:** `bmad-bmm-*` | **Workflows in:** `_bmad/bmm/workflows/`

| Phase | Skills | Natural Language Triggers |
|-------|--------|--------------------------|
| **1-Analysis** | `technical-research`, `domain-research`, `market-research` | "research X", "investigate Y", "what are the options for Z" |
| **2-Planning** | `create-prd`, `edit-prd`, `validate-prd`, `create-product-brief`, `create-architecture`, `create-ux-design` | "create a PRD", "design the architecture", "plan the UX" |
| **3-Solutioning** | `create-epics-and-stories`, `create-story`, `sprint-planning`, `sprint-status` | "break this into stories", "plan the sprint", "check sprint status" |
| **4-Implementation** | `dev-story`, `quick-dev`, `quick-spec`, `code-review` | "implement story X", "quick fix", "review this code" |
| **Cross-cutting** | `check-implementation-readiness`, `correct-course`, `retrospective`, `document-project`, `generate-project-context` | "are we ready to build?", "course correct", "run retro", "document this project" |

### GDS — Game Development Studio
**Prefix:** `bmad-gds-*` | **Workflows in:** `_bmad/gds/workflows/`

| Phase | Skills | Natural Language Triggers |

## Routing Strategy: Natural Language → Skill

### Decision Tree (Priority Order)

```
User says something →
  1. EXACT MATCH: Does it match a slash command? → Execute directly
  2. LIFECYCLE PHASE: What phase of work is this?
     ├─ Research/Analysis → BMM research or CIS brainstorming
     ├─ Planning/Design → BMM PRD/Architecture or GDS Brief/GDD
     ├─ Implementation → BMM dev-story/quick-dev or spec workflow
     ├─ Testing → TEA testarch-* or test-fix
     ├─ Review → bmad-review-* or code-review
     └─ Maintenance → retrospect, correct-course, deploy, heal
  3. DOMAIN: Is this game dev? → GDS variant. General product? → BMM variant.
  4. META: Is this about BMAD itself? → BMB module
  5. CREATIVE: Is this ideation/innovation? → CIS module
  6. TOOL NEED: Does it need external data?
     ├─ Library docs → context7
     ├─ Research papers → cohezion-research
     ├─ GitHub code → github MCP
     ├─ Knowledge graph → cohezion-surreal
     └─ Multi-perspective → cohezion-swarm
```

## Pruning Recommendations

### Redundant / Consolidation Candidates

| Skill(s) | Issue | Recommendation |
|-----------|-------|----------------|
| `bmad-gds-create-game-brief` + `bmad-gds-game-brief` | Two skills for the same thing (one via MCP, one via command) | Keep command version, remove MCP duplicate |
| `bmad-gds-gdd` + `bmad-gds-create-gdd` | Same — GDD creation via two paths | Keep `create-gdd` (collaborative), deprecate `gdd` |
| `bmad-brainstorming` + `bmad-cis-brainstorming` + `superpowers:brainstorming` | Three brainstorming skills | Keep `bmad-brainstorming` (interactive workflow) + `superpowers:brainstorming` (meta-enhancer). Remove MCP `cis-brainstorming` |
| `bmad-bmm-code-review` + `bmad-gds-code-review` + `code-review:code-review` + `pr-review-toolkit:review-pr` | Four code review skills | Keep `bmad-bmm-code-review` (general) + `pr-review-toolkit:review-pr` (PR-specific). Remove `gds-code-review` unless actively building games. Remove `code-review:code-review` (subset of pr-review-toolkit) |
| `bmad-bmm-sprint-status` + `bmad-gds-sprint-status` | Duplicate sprint status for two domains | Keep BMM, alias GDS to it unless game project active |
| `bmad-bmm-retrospective` + `bmad-gds-retrospective` + `retrospect` | Three retro skills | Keep `retrospect` (dev-focused, flows into core files) + `bmad-bmm-retrospective` (product lifecycle). Remove GDS variant |
| `claude-api:*` + `document-skills:*` + `example-skills:*` | Three plugin namespaces with identical skills (pdf, docx, pptx, frontend-design, etc.) | These are the same skills from different marketplace plugins. Keep ONE namespace (recommend `document-skills:*`), remove the other two |

### Low-Value / Never-Used Candidates

| Skill | Reason | Recommendation |
|-------|--------|----------------|
| `bmad-bmb-validate-max-parallel-workflow` | Extremely niche — only for parallel workflow validation | Keep only if actively building BMAD modules |
| `bmad-gds-gametest-*` (6 skills) | Full game testing suite — irrelevant unless building games | Disable unless game project active |
| `bmad-agent-gds-*` (7 agents) | Game-specific agent personas | Same — disable unless game project |
| `hookify:writing-rules` | Meta-skill about writing hookify rules | Rarely needed; `hookify:hookify` covers creation |
| `ralph-loop:*` (3 skills) | Ralph Loop plugin — unclear if used | Evaluate usage; remove if unused |
| `sentry:*` (3 skills) | Sentry integration — only relevant if using Sentry | Keep dormant unless Sentry is configured |
| `huggingface-skills:*` (12 skills) | HuggingFace ecosystem — heavy, niche | Keep only if doing ML model work |

### Token Cost Analysis

The biggest token sinks from skill/command loading:
1. **BMAD commands** (~90): Each is tiny (3-6 lines), but they all appear in the skill listing, adding noise
2. **Triple-duplicate plugin skills** (claude-api + document-skills + example-skills): ~40 skills x3 = 120 entries for ~40 actual capabilities
3. **GDS module** (~20 skills): Full game dev pipeline that's dormant unless building games

**Estimated savings from pruning**: Remove ~60 redundant/dormant entries, reducing skill listing noise by ~40%.
